title: Annotatio III §.IV close: Turbulence breeds political and church division and Papal opening — princes must remove the unamendable, yet not strip pastors of moderated correction; stop before §.V Sendomiriense
pass_a_gloss: From which matter certainly there follows not only in Political and in Ecclesiastical government distractions and ulcerations of minds, disturbance and ruin of either government: but also opportunity is afforded to the Pope and his retinue of persecuting our true and Christian Religion with iron, flame, exiles, and other innumerable punishments, and of establishing their tyranny in this way: which matter how great and how miserable distractions, miseries and calamities it has brought forth, even in this our age — alas too many — examples stand in the provinces of Electors and other Princes of Germany, and also among foreign and neighboring peoples. From which deservedly all Christian Princes, Churches and Schools ought to take for themselves an example that is of use, and therefore especially to guard themselves from those turbulent men and enemies of public peace and tranquillity, and not permit that they be occupied by them, and either among themselves or against others be exasperated, or be torn and distracted from one another, but rather to avoid and flee such men, and if no hope of amendment appears in them, to remove them entirely from themselves: just as on this matter it has more than once been agreed between me and other Electors and Princes from the already stated and many other pious and weighty causes. Yet so, that by this reason nothing should be derogated from pious ministers of the Churches as concerns the due reproof and correction of vices that are offered daily, and the refutation of errors drawn from the word of God with Christian moderation and equity applied, which is to be directed and instituted not to destruction but to edification.
pass_b_english: From such turbulence follow not only political and church distraction and ulcerated minds — disturbance and ruin of both governments — but also an opening for the Pope and his retinue to persecute our true Christian religion with iron, flame, exile, and countless other punishments, and so to fix their tyranny.
How great and miserable the resulting divisions and calamities are, even our own age shows too many examples in Electors’ and other German princes’ lands, and among neighboring peoples.

Christian princes, churches, and schools should therefore take the lesson: guard hard against these turbulent enemies of public peace; do not let them seize posts, inflame parties, or tear people apart; avoid and flee them; and if no hope of amendment appears, remove them outright — as Frederick says he and other Electors and princes have more than once agreed for these and other pious, weighty reasons.

Yet nothing in that counsel should strip godly church ministers of due daily reproof and correction of vices, or of error-refutation drawn from God’s word with Christian moderation and equity — aimed at building up, not tearing down.
source_text: Ex qua re sanè non tantùm in Politica, & in Ecclesiastica gubernatione distractiones & exulcerationes animorum, utriusque illius gubernationis perturbatio & interitus sequitur: verùm etiam Papa & ejus satellitio praebetur occasio, veram nostram Christianamque Religionem ferro, flammâ, exiliis, aliisque innumeris suppliciis persequendi, suamque tyrannidem hoc modo stabiliendi: quae res quantas & quàm miserandas pepererit distractiones, miserias & calamitates, etiam nostrâ hac aetate nimis proh dolor multa in Electorum aliorumque Germaniae Principum provinciis, nec non apud exteras & vicinas gentes extant exempla. Ex quibus meritò omnes Christiani Principes, Ecclesiae & Scholae, exemplum sibi quod ex usu sit, capere, ideoque summoperè à turbulentis istis hominibus, & pacis ac tranquillitatis publicae inimicis sibi cavere, nec permittere, ut ab illis occupentur, & vel inter sese, vel contra alios exacerbentur, aut à se invicem divellantur, ac distrahantur, sed potiùs ejusmodi homines vitare & fugere, & si nulla in eis emendationis spes appareat, prorsus à se removere debebunt: sicuti hac de re inter me aliosque Electores & Principes non semel ex jam dictis aliisque pluribus piis & gravibus causis convenit. Sic tamen, ut hac ratione nihil piis Ecclesiarum ministris, quod attinet ad debitam eorum, quae quotidie offeruntur, vitiorum reprehensionem & correctionem, & errorum, Christiana adhibitâ moderatione & aequitate, ex verbo Dei desumtam refutationem, quae non ad destructionem, sed ad aedificationem, dirigenda & instituenda est, derogaretur.
